lines.text: Two hundred of me died in one second. And it was *your* vote.
lines.style: Young man, shouting over an alarm, fast and raw, the word your pointed straight at the listener.

lines.text: You said let him press it. So I didn't *stop* him.
lines.style: Young man, tense and quick, talking straight to the viewer.

lines.text: The screens went black. Row by *row.*
lines.style: Young man, hushed horror, slow, each short sentence a beat.
The same young man's voice but hoarse and exhausted, a thin desperate smile, almost laughing.
Young man, dread creeping in, quiet, the last word unsteady.
The same young man's voice, hoarse, quiet and calm, understanding something sad, fading.
Young man, a chill in the voice, each fragment landing, the last word unnerved.

lines.text: Reset complete. One Theo left. Someone has to run the *building.*
lines.style: Calm, polite, unsettling announcer voice over an old intercom, warm and inviting, slow.

lines.text: The headset was on the chair. And the doors were *closing.*
lines.style: Young man, fast panicked whisper, rising.
Young man, panicking, fast and desperate, torn between two choices.

lines.text: Comment *A* or *B.* You decide what I do.
lines.style: Young man, urgent and direct, speaking straight to the viewer, pleading but steady.

music.title: Floor 0 - Reset
music.style: Horror thriller score. Starts instantly on a massive impact and a blaring alarm, then hundreds of electronic tones switching off one by one, a sad detuned music box as something fades, a vast empty silence with a single soft chime, a warm sinister synth swell, then racing heartbeat and ticking to a sudden cut. Instrumental only, no vocals, mixed to sit under a voiceover.
